key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN, maximal at onset. LOCATION: Chest and/or BACK (interscapular). RADIATES along aortic path (chest→back→abdomen as dissection extends). DURATION: Continuous, persistent. CHARACTER: TEARING, RIPPING, or severe sharp pain. AGGRAVATING: Hypertension. RELIEVING: Nothing helps. TIMING: Sudden onset, unrelenting. SEVERITY: 10/10, catastrophic. KEY POSITIVES: Hypertension, pulse or BP differential between extremities, Marfan syndrome, bicuspid aortic valve, aortic regurgitation murmur. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT gradual onset, NOT pressure (like MI).
